title: Operations Overview – Sky Controls
prompt:
Create the Operations Overview screen showing the "Sky Control & Atmospheric Engine" fully expanded as an interactive modal / popover drawer over the dashboard.
Layout & Components:
1. Underneath, visible through frosted dark glass (rgba(18,18,19,0.7) blur 20px), is the Operations Overview screen.
2. The Sky Control panel is prominently opened:
   - Header: "Atmospheric Scene Engine" with subtitle "Deterministic NWP / Neural Gated Shader Preview" and an "Auto (Follows Forecast)" pill toggle (currently OFF / Manual Override).
   - Mode Switch: "Strict Monochrome" switch (toggle switch with caption: "When ON, locks --accent to #E9DFCB sand and removes condition color cues").
   - Ambient Intensity Slider: Sleek range slider from 0% to 100% set to 75% with tick marks (Subtle, Operational 35%, Cinematic 75%, Full 100%).
   - Ambient Motion Toggle: "Dynamic Physics & Particle Engine" (ON / OFF).
   - The 13 Scene Chips in a structured, clean grid or scrollable matrix showing all 13 required weather scenes:
     1. Snow (Flakes & frost vignette)
     2. Rain (Slanted streaks & ripples)
     3. Heavy Rain / Cloudburst (Dense deluge)
     4. Thunderstorm & Lightning (Active, selected with purple accent outline)
     5. Hot / Heatwave (Shimmer & sun glare)
     6. Cold / Cold Wave (Icy mist & frost dendrites)
     7. Clear / Sunny (Pale sun disc & rays)
     8. Cloudy (Stratified grey cloud banks)
     9. Fog / Haze (Low rolling mist strata)
     10. High Wind (Horizontal velocity streaks)
     11. Cyclone (Rotational vortex spiral)
     12. Dust Storm (Loess particle sweep)
     13. Night (Dark base & lunar ambient)
   - Each chip includes a miniature visual thumbnail / icon and condition label, with the active chip highlighted.
   - Live Caption preview below the slider: "Now showing: Thunderstorm · +48h · Manual Override".
3. Style: Refined dark command center, Syne display typography for titles, frosted glass panels with 1px border `rgba(255,255,255,0.12)`, tabular numbers, monochrome palette with only small accent touches.
